title: Release Day Ops Playlist and Staggered Backfill Plan (June release) - WIP
summary: Working draft of the day-of operations playlist (short, checklist-style actions), a staggered backfill plan to bring capacity online safely, and an initial release notes draft. Focus is operational clarity for a staged release with multiple dependent subsystems (serving runtime, routing, optimize service). Not final — intended for release leads and SRE on-call to iterate.
playlist_intent: Condensed, prioritized actions for T-60m through T+120m to minimize chatter and ensure deterministic handoffs. Use this as the single source of truth on release day for checklist status updates.
release_day_playlist:
T-60m: announce release start on #release-ops (Slack), confirm on-call roster and escalation path; verify preflight green (QA smoke, perf gate reports linked); advance canary cohort flags.

T-30m: deploy database migration if applicable behind feature flag; confirm migration telemetry and rollback window; snapshot relevant schemas.

T-15m: coordinate client teams (console, SDK, internal infra) that will trigger traffic; ensure throttles configured; enable increased sampling for traces.

T+0m: flip traffic to new release cohort (20% traffic by default) using routing policy; enable verbose tracing for cohort; post status in #release-ops with cohort id.

T+10m: run smoke tests (end-to-end chat flow, embeddings index sanity, long-sequence generation at 2x token length for 1 request) and sanity checks on latency SLOs; check error-rate and 95th pct latency.

T+30m: if green, increase to 60% using staggered backfill policy (see backfill plan); otherwise, trigger rollback checklist.

T+60m: full traffic ramp if metrics are stable and no regressions in quality metrics (prompt set checks).

T+120m: finalize release announcement, tag release in repo, schedule post-release retrospective check-in.

Note: At every step capture ETA and confirm the person who made the change in #release-ops. If any manual intervention occurs, open a short incident channel and assign an SRE lead.
staggered_backfill_plan:
Goal: bring additional serving capacity online gradually to avoid cache stampedes and prevent KV-store hotkeys from thrashing. Backfill operates in two dimensions: capacity (GPUs/pods) and model-variant coverage.

Phase A (canary to 20%): no backfill — validate model correctness and routing.

Phase B (20% -> 60%): enable staggered backfill of worker pools in 3 waves, 10 minutes apart. Each wave: spin up 25% of planned extra replicas, warm KV caches using synthetic warmup traffic, run targeted prefix-cache checks for top 100 prefixes from traffic sample. Verify latency tail and token throughput after each wave.

Phase C (60% -> 100%): remaining replicas in 2 waves, 15 minutes apart. Before final wave, run a scaled throughput test for 10 minutes at expected peak RPS to ensure batchers/kernels behave under load. If throughput drops or cold-start errors appear, pause and rollback last wave.

Backfill safety knobs:
- Autoscaler soft-caps to limit concurrent pod startups to 40% of cluster growth per 10m.
- KV-cache warming flag to avoid evicting hot prefixes for 30m after node addition.
- Rate-limiter fallbacks to route to dedicated nodes if host-level CPU > 85%.

Operators: annotate each wave with wave-id and owner in the orchestration UI and Slack message. If any wave causes error-rate delta > 0.5% or latency 95th increase > 15%, rollback that wave and notify SRE lead.

smoke_and_gate_checks:
Mandatory quick pass checks to call green/red:
- API correctness: sample responses for 10 canned prompts must match baseline output tokens (no catastrophic regressions).
- Latency gates: p50 < 80ms, p95 < 380ms for hosted API in test region.
- Error-rate: 5xx < 0.2% and delta < 0.5% vs baseline.
- Model quality: automated eval set (20 prompts) must not drop mean BLEU/ROUGE more than threshold defined in product QA.
- Observability: traces, logs, and cost telemetry flowing to Console; no missing metrics for > 5 minutes.
If any gate fails, step down to previous stable model and follow rollback section.
rollback_checklist:
Immediate steps if rollback is needed:
1) Announce rollback intent in #release-ops with reason and ticket reference.
2) Pause further traffic ramps and set routing to previous stable tag.
3) If model version rollback, invalidate new KV caches and warm old caches with synthetic warmup traffic.
4) Revert infra changes (feature flags, autoscaler tweaks) via orchestration UI.
5) Run focused smoke tests against stable tag and confirm metrics return to baseline.
6) Create incident issue (ENGREL-xxxx) and assign owners for root cause investigation.
7) Schedule hotfix release window if needed and notify stakeholders.
8) Postmortem trigger: any rollback lasting >30 minutes or customer-impacting event.

release_notes_draft:
(Draft - intended to be customer-facing after final review)
Title: June 2026 Platform Release — improved routing and cost controls
Highlights:
- Adaptive routing policies: finer-grained control over latency vs cost routing for multi-tenant traffic (ENGREL-7213).
- Improved kernel selection heuristics for long-context models, reducing p95 latency by ~12% in internal benchmarks (RFC in linked artifacts).
- New backfill safety knobs to prevent cache thrash during scale events.
Bug fixes:
- Fixed intermittent KV-store eviction causing tokenization mismatches for high-prefix traffic (ENGINFRA-1349).
- Addressed a memory leak in batch aggregator observed under synthetic load.
Known issues:
- SDK telemetry sampling may show temporary duplicate traces in rare edge cases — fix in next minor release.
Upgrade notes:
- No customer action required for hosted API. Dedicated customers with pinned versions should coordinate with Solutions Engineering for a private rollout schedule.
Contact: support@redwood.ai for questions or to schedule an enterprise rollout window.
